solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Giant mushrooms no good for muscle

indicators.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good, and 'no' tells us to drop it from the words before

parts.note: giant means big
ceps are a kind of edible wild mushroom (porcini)

explanation.surface: Eating enormous mushrooms will do nothing for your muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' removes the G from BIG CEPS, leaving the muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps is the large muscle at the front of the upper arm.

clue.text: Wicked party game for swingers?

parts.note: base means morally low, wicked
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: A naughty party game for wife-swappers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swingers' suggests partner-swapping, but batters swing at the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball players swing a bat at the pitched ball, so they are literally swingers.

clue.text: Pervert to produce contented sound climbing into bed

indicators.note: into puts the reversed sound inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means read upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: a purr is a cat's contented sound

explanation.surface: To corrupt someone, purr your way up into their bed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' means read upwards, giving RRUP; 'into' sets it inside the small bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pervert or corrupt is to lead astray morally, debasing something good.

clue.text: Film of feature length, perhaps fix copies in state

parts.note: to pin is to fix in place

indicators.note: in places the copies within the state's name

parts.note: Ohio is a US state
cc stands for carbon copies

explanation.surface: A full-length movie; perhaps fix the copies in a particular state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature length' is a film term but also the nose, which grew when Pinocchio lied.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's Pinocchio is a feature-length film whose title character is known for nose length.

clue.text: Vicious Scotsman pursuing alumnus produces glass

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the Scotsman's pieces come after the alumnus

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil
Sid Vicious was the Sex Pistols' bassist
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A cruel Scot chasing a former schoolmate somehow makes glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vicious' looks like an adjective but points to the punk musician Sid Vicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsidian is a dark natural volcanic glass formed when lava cools rapidly.

clue.text: Enemy takes both manoeuvres similarly

indicators.note: manoeuvres means moves around, so these letters are repositioned

explanation.surface: The enemy captures both sides by moving in the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces a parallel point that follows for the same reason, likewise.

clue.text: Arab or Irish-American taking first question?

parts.note: IR is Irish and A is American, joined as the hyphen suggests
I is one, the first number

explanation.surface: Is that man an Arab, or an Irish-American quizzed first?
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Iraq is an Arab, Iraq being an Arab country.

clue.text: Politician appears in Oldie that's reviewed collapse

indicators.note: appears in places the politician inside the rearranged letters
reviewed suggests looking over and recasting, so the letters of Oldie are reordered

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP shows up in a review in The Oldie magazine about a collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oldie is a British humorous magazine; 'reviewed' makes ILODE, and 'appears in' slots the politician after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To implode is to cave in violently on itself.

clue.text: Change in US prison essential after evacuation

parts.note: the nick is British slang for a prison or police station

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, leaving only the outside letters of essential

explanation.surface: Change is vital in America's prisons once they have been cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in US' seems to place the prison in America; it actually belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickel is the American five-cent coin, a piece of small change.

clue.text: One offering vision of what may come to pass

definitions.text: One offering vision of what may come to pass

parts.words: One offering vision of what may come to pass
parts.note: sounds like a prophet foretelling events, but means a device showing vehicles behind that may overtake

explanation.definitionFit: A driver's mirror shows traffic approaching from behind that might soon overtake.

clue.text: Tight cord flexed when first pulled

parts.note: a cord is a string

indicators.note: the first letter is pulled away from the word for flexed

parts.note: flexed means bent

explanation.surface: A taut cord is bent once it has been tugged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when first pulled' strips the B from BENT, leaving ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent rules are strict, tightly drawn and leaving no slack.

clue.text: Stock set with food as image shows

parts.note: pic is short for picture, an image

explanation.surface: A savoury jelly set around food, as the photograph shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, set around pieces of food.

clue.text: Lively ball requires tough doorman

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a short-pitched delivery that rears up at the batsman
a burly man who keeps unwanted people out of a club

explanation.surface: A bouncy ball needs a hard man on the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb to bounce: a ball bouncing high, and throwing troublemakers out.

clue.text: Ultimately servile brute — United follower?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word servile

parts.note: a pig is a brutish person or beast
united means made one

explanation.surface: A slavish thug is apparently a Manchester United fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United follower' suggests a football supporter, but United is ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigone is an imitative disciple or successor of a great artist or thinker.

clue.text: Churchill at Chartwell stays closer to door

indicators.note: the word stays inside the phrase Churchill at Chartwell, held within its letters

explanation.surface: Churchill remains at his home Chartwell, closer to the door.
explanation.walkthrough: Chartwell was Churchill's country house in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is a fastening that holds a door closed.

clue.text: Dine out to entertain three kings in dream

definitions.note: used as an adjective, as in a dream holiday: fancied, not real

indicators.note: to entertain means to hold as a guest, so the kings go inside
out signals that the letters of dine are put out of order

parts.note: the Magi were the three kings of the Nativity

explanation.surface: Dining out with three kings happens only in a dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' gives INED, and 'to entertain' has that hold the kings; 'dream' works as an adjective, as in a dream home.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreamt up exists only in the mind, conjured by fancy rather than reality.

clue.text: Hassle as government department cuts pay

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the department goes inside the pay

parts.note: income is pay
MOD is the Ministry of Defence

explanation.surface: It's a nuisance when a ministry slashes your wages.
explanation.definitionFit: To incommode is to inconvenience or trouble someone, putting them out.

clue.text: Sleeping place for baby at home that dog must guard

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding, so the dog goes around the home letters

parts.note: a basset is a short-legged hound
in means at home

explanation.surface: The family dog must watch over the baby's cot at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassinet is a hooded basket-like cradle for an infant.

clue.text: Dry grass now transported, brought to the old Welsh town

parts.note: hay is grass cut and dried

indicators.note: transported means moved about, so the letters of now are rearranged

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: Hay and other goods are carted to an old town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' turns NOW into ONW.
explanation.definitionFit: Hay-on-Wye is a small town on the Welsh border, famous for second-hand bookshops.

clue.text: Rancid meal in time causes illness

indicators.note: rancid means gone off, spoiled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eating spoiled food in time makes you ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rancid' rearranges MEAL and IN into AILMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is a minor sickness or disorder.

clue.text: Punch adult companion

parts.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Hitting a grown-up who happens to be a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA means a mate from Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate.
explanation.definitionFit: In British rhyming slang a china is a friend or mate.

clue.text: Understanding current things differently

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: differently means arranged another way, so the letters of things are reordered

explanation.surface: To understand modern matters you must see them in a new way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges THINGS into NSIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep, intuitive grasp of a situation.

clue.text: Article about Langley people in plant

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
ca is circa, about
the CIA has its headquarters at Langley, Virginia

explanation.surface: A report about CIA people planting a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a mole in espionage; here it is a botanical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia is a genus of trees and shrubs, including wattles.

clue.text: Conservative lives alone in retreat for notables

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so these words are read in reverse

parts.note: lives means is, exists
solo means alone

explanation.surface: A Tory lives on his own in a hideaway for celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns IS SOLO into OLOSSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi, giants, are figuratively people of towering importance or renown.

clue.text: Don't talk about fate or sin

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hush goes around fate

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about destiny or wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth, laziness, is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Old southern lawgiver one for eastern assimilation

indicators.note: one replacing another: one stands in for eastern within the lawgiver's name

parts.note: Moses brought down the Ten Commandments
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ancient southern lawmaker absorbs eastern ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one for eastern' swaps the second E of MOSES for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is figuratively the gradual, unconscious absorption of ideas or knowledge.

clue.text: Belief choirmaster's beginning to repeat

indicators.note: beginning picks out the opening letter of choirmaster's

parts.note: to redo is to repeat

explanation.surface: A choirmaster believes in starting again from the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The Credo is also a sung part of the Mass, fitting the choir.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of faith or guiding principles, from Latin for I believe.

clue.text: Possibly regal English employed in socialist newspaper

indicators.note: employed in puts the English letter to work inside the word for socialist

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist
an organ is a newspaper or journal serving as a mouthpiece

explanation.surface: Perhaps royal Englishmen work at a left-wing paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regal' is not royal: a regal is a small portable reed organ of the Renaissance.
explanation.definitionFit: A regal is an example, a small portable keyboard instrument with beating reeds.

clue.text: Leander certainly wasn't this central character

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly for love of Hero, so he was hardly opposed to her
a protagonist lacking conventional heroic qualities

explanation.surface: Leander was no unheroic lead, but no enemy of Hero either.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero was the priestess Leander loved, so read as ANTI-HERO he was certainly not that.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a protagonist who lacks traditional virtues such as courage or morality.

clue.text: Players notice team's leader training inside

indicators.note: inside places the training letters within the word for notice

parts.note: to notice is to see
PT is physical training

indicators.note: the leader of team's is its first letter

explanation.surface: Musicians spot their team captain working out indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts the physical training within the word for notice; 'leader' supplies the T at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A septet is a group of seven musicians performing together.
